sentences: Heat the butter in a small frying pan over a low heat with the thyme and ½ tsp freshly ground black pepper until the butter begins to foam.
Heat the oven to 170C/150C fan/gas 3½.
Whisk the egg yolks in a large bowl with 20g of the sugar, the flour, oil, milk, baking powder and vanilla extract until just combined, being careful not to overmix.
Generously oil a 20cm angel food cake tin, or a 22-23cm bundt or ring tin.
Sieve the flour and ¼ tsp fine salt into a mixing bowl, then add the cooled melted ghee.
Divide and shape the dough into 17-18 balls about 20g each and roughly 3cm in diameter.
Roll out each ball on a lightly oiled surface to a circle about 10cm in diameter (the pastry will be thinner if the balls are rolled out individually).
Heat the oil in a wok or karahi over a medium heat to 130°C or until a cube of bread dropped in browns in 1 min.
Put the eggs in a single layer in a pan and add enough water to cover them by 2cm.
Put the different food colourings into separate bowls or containers that will hold the eggs, using 1 tsp food colouring per bowl, plus 700ml water and 1 tbsp of the vinegar each.
Add the mayonnaise, adding a little more if you need to in order to create a slightly stiff paste, then mix in 3 tbsp of the chopped pepper and the tarragon, if using.
Heat oven to 160C/140C fan/gas 3.
Grease and line the base and sides of 3 x 20cm cake tins with baking parchment.
Season the turkey all over, including under the skin, with 1-2 tbsp flaky sea salt.
Heat the oven to 200C/180C fan/gas 6.
Perfection is when the thickest part of the breast is about 65C and the thickest part of the thigh is 75C.
With the motor still running, add the sugar 1 tbsp at a time, allowing it to be incorporated before adding the next.
Pour the milk and 200ml water into a wide pan or medium frying pan and heat until steaming, but not boiling.
To make the caramel, heat the sugar, 1 tbsp water and pinch of salt in a small pan and cook on a medium heat until you get a lightly golden caramel, about 10 mins.
Heat oven to 200C/180C fan/gas 6.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large pan.
Add the onions with a pinch of salt, and cook until translucent, around 3-4 mins.
Stir in the beans, cumin, chilli powder, oregano, some seasoning and 100ml water.
Line 4 small pudding-shaped moulds (200ml capacity) with cling film, smoothing it over to fit snugly, leaving an overhang around the edge.
Squeeze 3 tbsp of juice and put it in a pan with the rum and sugar.
Measure off 4 tbsp of the fruit and its syrup, and set aside in a rigid freezer container (freeze for up to a month).
Melt the white chocolate and, using a teaspoon, drizzle 4 star shapes over the pencil outlines.
Heat oven to 220C/200C fan/gas 7.
Pour in the milk and stir in 100g of the cheese, stirring until melted.
Heat the oven to 180C/160C fan/gas 4.
Oil and line a 20cm round springform, deep tin so that the parchment comes 5cm above the rim.
For the streusel, mix together the flour, sugar, cinnamon and a pinch of salt in a large bowl.
Slice the bottom 2cm of the asparagus spears into thin rounds and set aside in a bowl with the lemon juice.

Add the asparagus to the tray and toss in 1 tbsp of the olive oil, season and grill for 10-15 mins, turning halfway through, until the potatoes are crisp and the asparagus is cooked through and a little charred.
Heat the oven to 200C/180C fan/gas 6.
Heat the oven to 200C/ fan 180/gas 6.
Drizzle over 2 tbsp olive oil and shake the tin to coat the potatoes.
Oil and line the base and sides of a 23cm springform cake tin.
Beat the egg yolks and 50g of the caster sugar in another bowl until pale and thickened, around 5 mins.
Gently fold the whisked yolk mixture into the chocolate mixture along with the chopped hazelnuts and a pinch of sea salt.
If not freezing the cake, heat the oven to 180C/160C fan/gas 4 and bake for 35-45 mins.
Heat the oven to 200C/180C fan/gas 6.
Line a 20cm square baking tin with baking parchment and set aside.
Reduce the oven to 180C/160C fan/gas 4.
Tip the sweet potato mix into a bowl and combine with all the remaining ingredients, except the almonds and 50g of the dark chocolate.
Heat the oven to 170C/150C fan/gas 3 and line the base of a deep 20cm cake tin with baking parchment or a reusable baking liner, then butter the sides of the tin.
Combine the onion, vinegar, sugar and a pinch of salt in a small non-reactive bowl and set aside.
Stir through the soy, fish sauce, brown sugar, lime juice and 1 tbsp water.
Heat the oven to 110C/ 100C fan/gas ¼.
Now turn the speed up and start to add 115g caster sugar, a dessertspoonful at a time.
Sift one third of the 115g icing sugar over the mixture, then gently fold it in with a big metal spoon or rubber spatula.
